web_evidence.title: Excerpt from A Day Late and A Dollar Short by Terry McMillan
web_evidence.note: A sustained excerpt reprinted with Viking Books’ permission opens with Viola narrating her own circumstances and family relationships as “I.”

web_evidence.title: A Day Late and a Dollar Short by Terry McMillan
web_evidence.note: This EBSCO/Magill’s structural analysis explicitly identifies six first-person narrators: Viola, Cecil, and their four children.

web_evidence.title: A Day Late and a Dollar Short Reader’s Guide
web_evidence.note: The publisher guide describes each Price speaking in an individual voice, calls them the novel’s six narrators, and includes first-person reflections from several of them.

web_evidence.title: Delicious Family Saga Finds Terry McMillan in Top Form
web_evidence.note: The review describes six distinctive voices and successive narrators, while quoting Viola’s participating first-person narration.

web_evidence.title: Better Late Than Never / Seven years after her mother's death, McMillan finishes her novel of family dynamics
web_evidence.note: The review states that the novel comprises alternating chapters narrated by the individual family characters and discusses the characters’ distinct narratorial voices.

person_note: The supplied quotes are all gnomic sayings and provide no base-narrator evidence. The authorized opening independently demonstrates Viola’s first-person narration, while EBSCO explicitly establishes that the whole novel uses six first-person narrators. Publisher and major-review descriptions corroborate the multi-narrator chapter structure. Because every sustained narrator uses first person, the changing narrators do not make the book ALTERNATING under the methodology. No credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person sections was found.
